video.title: I Built an AI Agent in 5 Minutes (And Sold It Live)

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates a campaign to sell AI voice agents to local service businesses, using ringless voicemail drops to contact tree-care companies. He shows lead selection, campaign setup, several callbacks, and a GoHighLevel voice-agent build. The campaign generated calls and conversations, but the transcript does not report a sale. His main takeaway is that the agent is quick to build; finding customers and handling follow-up are the harder parts.

ideas.name: AI voice-agent setup for local service businesses
ideas.one_liner: Build and install AI voice agents that answer calls and collect job details for local service businesses.
ideas.business_model: Recurring monthly service fee for setting up and providing AI voice agents; the agent can answer calls, gather details, and notify the business team.
ideas.customer: Local service business owners, especially operators who are often driving or working on jobs and may miss calls. Examples discussed include tree-trimming, HVAC, pool-service, and similar businesses.
ideas.problem: Businesses can miss valuable calls when owners or staff are out working, driving, or otherwise unable to answer.
ideas.offer: Create an AI agent that answers inbound calls, uses a business knowledge base to respond to questions, collects contact and job information, and passes the details to the team. Chris also proposes selling a trained template through the HighLevel app marketplace.

pricing.model: Monthly recurring fee; Chris also offers to set up an agent for one prospect for free.

price_points.label: Price Chris says business owners may pay for an AI voice agent
Free setup offered to a prospect during the live call

pricing.notes: No customer accepted a paid offer in the transcript. The monthly price is stated as a potential price, not a closed sale.

acquisition_channels.details: Chris uploaded a brief recorded pitch and a list of tree-service phone numbers to Slide Broadcast, which sent ringless voicemail drops. He used Google Voice for callbacks. He reports calls from recipients, including some who had not heard the voicemail. UK legal applicability of this outbound method is a concern.

quote.text: I'm going to show you my phone, my Google Voice account, and I'm going to send ringless voicemail drops to 500 business owners, wait for them to call me back, and try to close a deal for an AI voice agent.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Chris mentions cold calls as one possible additional touch, but does not demonstrate making outbound cold calls in this campaign. He answers calls from prospects who call him back.
Chris recommends email as one possible additional touch in a multi-channel campaign; he does not send email in the demonstrated campaign.
Chris lists LinkedIn outreach as another possible touch; he does not demonstrate using it in the campaign.

ideas.delivery: Configure a voice agent in GoHighLevel, choose its voice and response settings, and give it a knowledge base built from a business website or generated and edited with ChatGPT. The agent answers inbound calls, collects details such as name, address, phone number, and issue, then emails the information to the business team. The provider handles setup and may connect a new or ported-in phone number. Any physical service work and on-site quotes remain with the client business.
unit_economics_claims: Chris says businesses may pay USD 500–2,000 per month for an AI voice agent; no paid customer or margin is reported.
Chris says he can build the agent in about five minutes or less, and later says the demonstration took about three minutes.
Chris offered one prospect a free setup, but the prospect did not accept a definite project.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated for launching the agent service. Chris says a self-run Outscraper scrape cost about USD 4; free lead lists were also available through his group.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. The campaign produced callbacks and conversations, but no sale is reported.

acquisition.how: Lead scraping and voicemail sending can be software-assisted, but list selection, offer creation, callbacks, and closing were human-led. Chris's demonstrated cold voicemail method would need a legally compliant alternative in the UK; inbound marketing or compliant outreach to corporate subscribers could be more automatable.

onboarding.how: A web crawler or AI can draft the knowledge base, and templates can speed configuration. A person still needs to check the client's services, contact details, phone routing, and agent behavior.

delivery.how: The agent can handle routine inbound calls and collect details without a person on each call. A human is still needed to review edge cases, confirm availability, and perform any on-site quoting or service work.

billing.how: The transcript does not describe billing or an automated subscription setup, so recurring billing would need to be arranged and checked by a person.

support.how: Routine questions may be handled by the agent, but the transcript does not show a support process for client issues, failures, or changes to the agent.

uk_applicability.notes: The core voice-agent service can work for UK trades and other local businesses. The US ringless voicemail campaign should not be copied without legal review: UK rules restrict unsolicited automated marketing calls, and contact data and call handling also need appropriate privacy compliance. Pricing, phone-number setup, and the chosen outreach channels may need adaptation.

risks: The demonstrated ringless voicemail campaign is not shown to close a paid sale; callbacks can be accidental or low-intent.
Some recipients may be angry or confused by unsolicited outreach, and Chris reports that some people were angry.
UK rules restrict unsolicited automated marketing calls; screening against a do-not-call list alone does not establish compliance.
The agent can sound robotic or provide inappropriate answers if its voice, knowledge base, or settings are poorly chosen.
A business may still need human follow-up to confirm availability, quote jobs, and perform physical work.
Chris says a single standalone marketing touch may not produce strong results; multiple touches may help, but those channels have their own legal requirements.

tactics.name: Choose a niche and check demand
steps: Start with a service niche that has a clear missed-call problem; Chris considered pool-service and tree-trimming businesses.
Use Google Trends to compare search interest for related services over time.
Compare related terms, such as gutter cleaning and gutter repair, and use the Google Keyword Tool to check local search demand and keyword bidding competition.
Treat higher search interest as a clue about demand, not proof of profit or low competition.

quote.text: No, it's like there could be even more um supply to meet this demand. And this could be the most saturated category.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Scrape and prepare a focused lead list
steps: Search for relevant business categories and locations in Outscraper; Chris selected three pool-related categories for one example, then used already-cleaned tree-trimming leads for the live campaign.
Filter for businesses with phone numbers and set a maximum results count based on the number of campaign credits available.
Use existing free lead lists when available; Chris says his group lets members request them through Typeform.
If scraping directly, compare the estimate with the stated cost and turnaround time; Chris reports paying about USD 4 for the displayed list.
Keep only the fields needed for the campaign, then remove blanks and invalid numbers.
Randomize lead order in Google Sheets before taking a sample, to reduce location or alphabetical-order bias.

quote.text: And so whatever I'm doing, even if it's probably already randomized, I like taking 10 seconds and randomizing them again just in case.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Keep lead cleaning proportional to the value of the data
steps: Prioritize the first phone number in the scrape rather than spending extensive time checking every extra phone-number column.
Upload lists to Slide Broadcast's list manager to add a cell-versus-landline column, even without running a campaign.
Treat the added classification as a second check; Chris says the scrape data and validation are not perfectly accurate.

quote.text: because like if you can scrape unlimited leads for next to nothing, like why spend a bunch of time cleaning and scrubbing and validating a bunch of stuff.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Write a short voicemail around one customer pain
steps: Keep the message brief because Chris expects many recipients to listen for only a few seconds.
Lead with a problem that fits the niche, such as missing calls while working on a tree job.
Personalize only with information actually known about the prospect; in this example Chris knew they owned a tree-trimming business in Texas.
Give a clear callback instruction and use a callback voicemail greeting that matches the offer.

quote.text: We want to speak to a painoint. We want to solve a problem. We want to personalize as much as we can.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Prepare to answer callbacks
steps: Set the callback number and voicemail greeting before sending the campaign.
Turn off call screening and check that the number will ring as intended.
Avoid sending all messages at once if the operator cannot answer the callbacks; Chris says he would normally throttle the campaign.
Treat callbacks as an opening for a conversation, not proof that a prospect heard the pitch or wants to buy.

quote.text: Now, if I were being like responsive and dutiful, I would not let these go to voicemail. I would answer all of them and I would throttle them to not send 500 all at once because I want to be able to answer these calls because that's how you're going to close it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test a multi-touch sequence
steps: Use a voicemail drop as one touch rather than assuming a single message will produce strong results.
Test other appropriate channels, such as email, a call, or LinkedIn, and track which combination produces meaningful conversations.
The audience participant reports a sequence of voice note, email, then text; Chris says he would test it, but the transcript does not establish UK legal compliance for those touches.

quote.text: But like like any marketing, you want multiple touches and preferably you want multiple touches in different mediums.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build an initial voice-agent knowledge base quickly
steps: Create an agent with a clear name, language, voice, and initial greeting.
Use ChatGPT to draft a simple knowledge base for common questions and the intended next step, such as arranging an on-site quote.
Add the client's website to the HighLevel web crawler to pull in existing FAQs and business information.
Review the generated material, connect the knowledge base, choose the information to collect, and test the agent with a realistic call.
Use an email notification to pass completed call details to the business team.

quote.text: I'm building a simple AI voice agent to receive inbound calls at a tree trimming business called Chris's tree trimming. It needs to answer typical questions about scheduling an on-site quote for a trimming or removal job.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a template or marketplace to reduce setup friction
steps: Start from a tested agent template when one fits the client rather than building every configuration from scratch.
For clients already using HighLevel, consider selling or installing the agent through the HighLevel app marketplace.
Use a new HighLevel number or port the business's existing number, depending on the client's setup.

quote.text: And it, let's say you want to sell what I just built to other treeing business owners that are using High Level for themselves. You can sell it on the uh Highle um app marketplace.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Check legal requirements for the chosen outreach method in the target country; a US phone-number filter is not a substitute for UK marketing compliance.

evidence_quality.rationale: Chris gives a detailed first-hand walkthrough of lead preparation, campaign setup, callbacks, and an agent build. The campaign results are anecdotal, some send statistics are interim or inferred, and no paid sale or customer outcome is reported.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes Playmakers, his private community, and GoHighLevel. He says GoHighLevel supports the channel and that he receives a small kickback from users who become paying customers through his referral link.
